lesson-intro.text: A fire hydrant is a stack of simple shapes: bands, a dome and a tall barrel. This one is open on a hot day. Watch the stack go up, then stack your own.

collar.text: Start with the collar near the top: a flat band with rounded ends.

dome.text: On the collar, a round dome with a ring and a nut on top. Two ribs curve down it.

barrel.text: The barrel hangs from the collar. On the left, its side bends round a short neck.

belt.text: Where the sides stop, a second band wraps round the barrel.

lower.text: Below the belt, the barrel ends in a gentle curve. A wide foot flares out under it.

side-line.text: A long line right of the middle makes the barrel look round.

right-nozzle.text: On the right, a nozzle: a short neck, a cap, and a smaller knob at the end.

left-nozzle.text: The left nozzle has the same cap and knob, turned toward you.

water.text: Water pours from the knob in a thick curve into a puddle. Two ripples float on it.

stones.text: Last, three paving stones on the ground, each a slab with rounded corners.

red.text: Color the hydrant red: the dome, the ring, the barrel and both necks.

blue.text: Blue for the water and the puddle.

gray.text: Gray for the caps and knobs, the foot and the three stones.

cream.text: Cream for the nut, the collar and the belt.

lesson-outro.text: Your hydrant is gushing away. Would you splash in that puddle?
